channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Deputado bolsonarista que desejou morte de Lula vira réu no STF
item.description: Bolsonarist deputy Gilvan da Federal (PL-ES) was made a defendant by the First Chamber of the STF for wishing the death of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva during a Chamber of Deputies session last year. The ruling marks a rare case of criminal liability for hate speech against the head of state in Brazil.

item.title: Primeiro compromisso de Flávio é revisitar reforma tributária, diz Alfredo Gaspar
item.description: Federal Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL), running mate on Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) ticket, stated that Flávio's first commitment, if elected, would be to 'revisit' the tax reform approved in 2023. The remark was made on Tuesday, the 18th, signaling an economic priority for a potential Bolsonaro administration.

item.title: Líder da oposição cobra da PGR oitiva de Lulinha
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber of Deputies, Cabo Gilberto Silva, filed a representation with the Attorney General's Office (PGR) urging urgent measures against Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, son of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, including the possibility of a hearing. The action is part of investigations into alleged irregularities involving the businessman.

item.title: Carlos Viana pede a Mendonça oitiva de Lulinha
item.description: Senator Carlos Viana (PSD-MG), former president of the INSS CPMI, requested that Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça evaluate a possible hearing of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, son of President Lula. The request follows the emergence of messages exchanged between Lulinha and others allegedly involved in irregularities within the INSS CPMI.

item.title: Primeira Turma do STF torna deputado réu por desejar a morte de Lula
item.description: The First Chamber of the Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) has made federal deputy Gilvan da Federal (PL-ES) a defendant in a case of insult after he publicly stated he wished for President Lula's death during a Public Security Committee session in April 2023. The ruling followed the rapporteur Minister Cármen Lúcia's vote and rejected the defense's claim that the remarks were protected by parliamentary immunity.

item.title: Alcolumbre assina despacho e avança com PEC do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre signed a dispatch to advance the PEC proposing the end of the 6×1 work schedule, following a rapprochement with President Lula. The document was sent to the Senate’s CCJ but is not yet visible in the system due to the parliamentary recess. The move reflects Alcolumbre’s effort to align with the federal government on key issues.

item.title: Primeira Turma do STF torna réu o deputado Gilvan da Federal por fala em que deseja morte de Lula
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) unanimously ruled to make federal deputy Gilvan da Federal (PL-ES) a defendant after he stated in a Public Security Committee meeting that he wanted President Lula to die and 'go to the fifth hell'. The court rejected his parliamentary immunity claim, ruling the statements constituted qualified insult directly targeting Lula’s person, unrelated to his official duties.

item.title: Flávio promete quatro ministros do STF contra aborto e drogas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL presidential candidate, pledged to appoint four Supreme Court justices aligned with opposition to abortion and drug legalization if elected in 2026. The statement was made in Belo Horizonte during a campaign event with allies in Minas Gerais.

item.title: O plano da Vale para fazer a mineração explodir no Brasil e gerar milhões de empregos
item.description: Vale presented the report 'Unlocking Mining Potential in Brazil', developed with Accenture, projecting 5.3 million jobs and R$1.3 trillion in tax revenue from 2026 to 2035 if its 15 proposals are adopted. The document covers environmental licensing, infrastructure, energy, regulation, and social impact, and will be delivered to 2026 presidential candidates.

item.title: Zema promete acabar com bets se for eleito presidente
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate from the Novo party, pledged to ban online betting platforms (bets) in Brazil if elected, stating it would be his first act in office. He made the announcement during a meeting with women affected by gambling addiction in São Paulo, describing betting platforms as harmful to society.

item.title: Augusto Cury troca de marqueteiro na primeira semana de campanha
item.description: Augusto Cury, the Presidential candidate for the Avante party, announced on Tuesday (18) the replacement of his campaign's chief marketer, hiring Sérgio Lima, a former advisor to Jair Bolsonaro in 2019 during the attempt to create the Aliança pelo Brasil party. The change took place in the first official week of the campaign, which began on Sunday (16), and includes the restructuring of press and communications teams. Cury currently stands at 2% in voting intentions according to a Quaest poll released on August 14.

item.title: A aliados, Alcolumbre diz que caso Messias é tema superado e que novo capítulo nem está no radar
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre says the Jorge Messias case — whose AGU leadership nomination to the STF was rejected by the Senate — is a closed matter, signaling openness to reconciliation with Lula. Although Lula has indicated he may resend Messias’s name for a new vote, Alcolumbre’s allies state this new chapter is not on the radar, reflecting efforts to move past the institutional crisis between the Executive and Legislative branches.

item.title: Flávio anuncia equipe com nomes pró-mercado no setor de energia
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro strengthened his campaign team with pro-market figures in the energy sector, including economist Adriano Pires, a public advocate for Petrobras privatization and market-based pricing, and lawyer Alexandre Chequer, a global energy law expert who helped structure Brazil’s petroleum framework and ANP. The team also includes former Minister of Mines and Energy Adolfo Sachsida leading the economic plan, alongside ex-Goldman Sachs executive Carolina Ragazzi and Lyvia Montezano, who leads the 'Brasil por Elas' initiative. The group aims to detail and present government proposals focused on reducing the state, implementing a new spending cap, and reviving privatizations and concessions.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que "não vai tolerar" desvios nas instituições de polícia
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas stated he will not tolerate misconduct in police institutions, emphasizing the role of the Internal Affairs and State Controller’s Office in fighting corruption. He advocated for transparency, inter-agency integration, and reinforced anticorruption goals, referencing the removal of the PM commander following an investigation. He also discussed education, housing, and the approach to Cracolândia, focusing on autonomy and health-based treatment.

item.title: Fachin critica discurso político de quem prega ‘demolição de instituições’
item.description: Minister Edson Fachin, president of the STF and CNJ, criticized political discourse that uses the 'demolition of institutions' as a method, particularly in attacks on the Judiciary. He released a booklet to explain magistrates' indemnity payments ('penduricalhos'), clarifying they do not increase patrimony but compensate for damages. Fachin stressed the need to separate the 'chaff from the wheat' in the judiciary, noting that control and transparency measures have already been implemented by the National Justice Corregedory.

item.title: Manifesto com artistas e políticos apoia candidatura de Dirceu
item.description: Former Minister José Dirceu launched a manifesto with 113 signatories, including artists like Alessandra Negrini and Gilberto Gil, and politicians like José Sarney and Marta Suplicy, supporting his candidacy for the Chamber of Deputies from São Paulo. The document highlights his trajectory in the military dictatorship resistance, the PT, and the Lula and Dilma governments, while defending his experience and commitment to democracy and social justice, despite campaign restrictions due to lymphoma treatment.

item.title: Pablo Marçal corrige declaração de R$ 7 bilhões em bens ao TSE e diz ter na verdade R$ 149 milhões
item.description: Presidential candidate Pablo Marçal (PRTB) requested a correction of his asset declaration to the TSE, fixing a typographical error that had reported R$7.4 billion instead of the correct R$149.99 million. The bulk of his declared assets now comes from corporate holdings, particularly an 80% stake in Aviation Participações Ltda. valued at R$80 million. Despite being ineligible until 2032 due to a prior conviction, Marçal obtained a preliminary injunction recognizing his PRTB affiliation, allowing him to register his candidacy while the TSE evaluates its validity until September 14.

item.title: Direita que sobrou é ruim e vota com a esquerda, diz Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate and co-founder of MBL, criticized the Brazilian right for becoming "very bad" and driven by social media influencers, abandoning economic reform agendas. He stated that right-wing congressmen voted alongside the left to reduce the workweek (end of the 6x1 scale), calling it a disgrace. Renan also denounced the Lula vs. Bolsonaro polarization, arguing the election is reduced to being "not Lula" or "not Bolsonaro" without substantive discussion of reforms or the country's economic future.

item.title: Candidato a suplente usa foto como Jesus Cristo e é intimado pelo TRE do Piauí a trocar imagem
item.description: Dilcon Afonso Santos Carvalho, a substitute candidate on the Christian Democracy (DC) ticket for Senate in Piauí, was ordered by the TRE-PI to replace his candidate registration photo, in which he appears dressed as Jesus Christ, for violating TSE Resolution No. 23.609/2019. The image was deemed non-compliant due to theatrical elements (crown of thorns and religious attire) that hinder voter recognition. He has until tomorrow to comply, or risk having his registration denied.

item.title: Por que Tarcísio não deve acompanhar a 1ª agenda de Flávio em SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas should not accompany Flávio Bolsonaro in the first campaign agendas in São Paulo on Thursday morning (08/20), as he will be attending a sabatina with CBN, Valor Econômico, and O Globo. Although allies suggest he may join Flávio later that day, the two are only expected to meet on Saturday (08/22) at the Festa do Peão de Barretos. This reflects a strategy of maintaining separate early campaign schedules for Flávio’s presidential bid.

item.title: Jovens perdem mais espaço no eleitorado, enquanto número de eleitores com mais de 60 anos cresce
item.description: The Brazilian electorate is aging: between 2010 and 2026, the number of eligible voters aged 16 to 24 dropped by 22%, from 24.7 million to 19.2 million, reducing their share of the total electorate from 18.2% to 12.5%. Despite this decline, young voters maintained high turnout in the 2022 elections, with 78.9% of 16–24-year-olds voting in the first round — and 16–17-year-olds (non-mandatory voters) showing the highest participation at 82.9%. The aging of the electorate is reshaping its composition, making elections more sensitive to small vote shifts.

item.title: Lula se afasta de Raquel Lyra em Pernambuco: ‘Quem vota em mim, vota em João Campos’
item.description: President Lula explicitly endorsed João Campos for governor of Pernambuco, stating that voting for him means voting for Campos, marking an electoral distancing from Governor Raquel Lyra despite maintaining good personal relations with both. Lula, who won nearly 70% of the vote in Pernambuco in 2022, reinforced his support for Campos, his PSB allied candidate, while Campos emphasized he is a 'friend' of Lula, contrasting Lyra as merely a 'colleague'. The governor avoided taking a clear stance in the presidential race, maintaining a centrist discourse with backing from PL figures and Bolsonaro-aligned figures.

item.title: Fernando Cerimedo é preso por suspeita de mandar matar companheira
item.description: Fernando Cerimedo, former advisor to Jair Bolsonaro and Javier Milei, was arrested in Bolivia on suspicion of ordering the attempted murder of his partner, Nadia Beller, who survived a close-range shooting in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. He was detained at Viru Viru Airport while attempting to return to Buenos Aires. The arrest sparked significant political repercussions in Bolivia due to his ties to President Rodrigo Paz’s government and his prominent role in Latin America’s far-right digital campaigns.

item.title: Romero Jucá desiste de concorrer a deputado federal por Roraima
item.description: Former Senator Romero Jucá (MDB) announced his withdrawal from the 2026 federal deputy race in Roraima, three days after having his eligibility restored by the STF. He claimed to be the target of lies, attacks on his public image, and an absurd and illegal judicial process, despite a prior acquittal. Jucá served as senator for Roraima for 24 years and held ministerial positions in the Lula and Temer administrations.

item.title: Feminicídio é “epidemia nacional”, diz Tarcísio sobre aumento em SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas labeled femicide a 'national epidemic' during a live interview on Record's Balanço Geral, after the state recorded 86 femicides in Q1 2026 — a 45% increase from 2025. Despite the rise, he noted that SP's rate (1.13 per 100,000 women) remains below the national average (1.42) and credited recent declines in indicators to public policies such as the Cabine Lilás program and electronic ankle monitors for aggressors.

item.title: PL tem 1 em cada 10 candidatos ao Senado; veja perfil de quem concorre ao cargo
item.description: The 2026 Senate elections feature 315 candidates for 54 seats, with the PL party leading at 33 candidacies (about 1 in 10). Female and Black candidate participation has increased since 2018, but the dominant profile remains white married men aged 50 or older.

item.title: “Se está habilitado, tem que concorrer”, diz Haddad sobre Marçal
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT candidate for governor of São Paulo, stated that Pablo Marçal has the right to run for president if regularized with the Electoral Justice, despite being ineligible until 2032. Haddad said he is a democrat and does not choose opponents, but that the debate should be based on defending the presidential legacy. Lula’s allies believe Marçal’s candidacy does not hurt Haddad’s performance, but is a detriment to politics overall.

item.title: ‘Bets acabam com o Brasil’, ‘não vale a pena ter bet’: Tarcísio e Haddad defendem proibição de aposta online no país
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) and Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans), rivals in the São Paulo gubernatorial race, both advocated for banning online betting (bets) in Brazil. They acknowledged that such a prohibition requires federal action by Congress and the president, as gambling regulation is national. Haddad said he would not license new betting activities if elected, while Tarcísio proposed mental health initiatives to combat gambling addiction, emphasizing its toll on productivity and household income.

item.title: Nogueira sugere a Kassab participar de eleição: “Fica falando bobagem”
item.description: Senator Ciro Nogueira, national president of the PP and candidate for re-election, suggested that Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD and vice-presidential candidate on Ronaldo Caiado's ticket, should run in a majoritarian election, claiming Kassab is 'talking nonsense' for saying the Centrão is aligned with Lula. The remark emerged amid tensions among government-aligned parties over the Centrão's political stance toward the federal administration.

item.title: Caiado apresenta plano para a Saúde com foco em prevenção, digitalização do SUS e prioridade na fila para doenças graves
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, presidential candidate for the PSD, unveiled a health plan centered on prevention, early diagnosis, SUS digitalization with a national electronic health record, and AI use in management and diagnostics, prioritizing severe cases in queues and restoring vaccination rates. Coordinated by former Health Minister Luiz Henrique Mandetta, the plan emphasizes regionalizing care to reduce avoidable deaths and draws from Caiado’s governance in Goiás, including his pandemic response. He reaffirmed his commitment to saving lives, citing his medical background and professional oath.

item.title: Flávio anuncia nomes do mercado e setor de infraestrutura para ajudar no programa de governo
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro announced names from the financial market and infrastructure sector to assist in shaping his government program. The move aims to strengthen the economic credibility of his campaign by involving figures with business and public works experience. The announcement was made on Tuesday, August 18, 2026.

item.title: Os motivos apresentados por Romero Jucá para não concorrer em 2026
item.description: Romero Jucá announced his withdrawal from the race for a federal deputy seat in Roraima for the 2026 elections, citing personal and family attacks as the main reason. He emphasized that, despite the suspension of his conviction for passive corruption and money laundering by Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino, the current political climate—marked by low and vicious disputes—led him to prioritize his family life and personal integrity. Jucá, a former 24-year senator and minister under Lula and Temer, stated that his public image had been attacked again, prompting him to reflect on his political future.

item.title: Após questionar dados da segurança e relatar intimidação da PM, Haddad acena a policiais em atos de campanha
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT candidate for governor of São Paulo, made overtures to police officers in two consecutive campaign events, promising salary improvements and modern technological equipment. He criticized Tarcísio de Freitas’ security management, disputing official data and highlighting an alleged police intimidation incident against a supporter, now under investigation by civil police and the Federal Prosecutor's Office.

item.title: Renan Santos defende fim da Justiça do Trabalho e da CLT
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão), a presidential candidate, advocated for abolishing the Labor Justice system and the CLT, proposing labor disputes be handled in regular courts and adopting an hourly work regime to reduce payroll costs. He denounced the proposal to reduce the workweek as 'madness', warning it would raise operational costs and lead to business closures and job losses. He emphasized his stance is principled, even if electorally costly, and made the remarks at an Unecs event in Brasília to align with the productive sector.

item.title: Veja o patrimônio de Marçal em declaração corrigida após apresentar R$ 7 bilhões em bens
item.description: Presidential candidate Pablo Marçal (PRTB) corrected his asset declaration after initially reporting R$ 7.4 billion, attributing the discrepancy to a typing error. The revised declaration shows a net worth of R$ 149.9 million, with major reductions in fixed-income investments (from R$ 6.7 billion to R$ 6.7 million) and a Santana de Parnaíba land parcel. Marçal remains ineligible until 2032, and his candidacy registration is pending review by the TSE.

item.title: Eleições 2026 têm 406 candidatos que se declaram LGBTQIA+
item.description: The 2026 elections feature 406 LGBTQIA+ candidates, representing 2% of the 20,575 total contenders. This is the first general election in which the TSE collected sexual orientation data during candidacy registration, with 11,334 candidates having responded. Although still below the estimated 12% of Brazil's LGBTQIA+ population (USP/UNESCO/IBGE, 2023), leaders like Gui Mohallem of Vote LGBT celebrate the progress since 2014, when such declarations were rare and politically risky.

item.title: Campanha de Renan Santos avalia ex-secretário do governo Lula para equipe econômica
item.description: The campaign of Renan Santos (Mission) is evaluating the inclusion of former Federal Budget Secretary Paulo Bijos in his future economic team, should he be elected. The information was disclosed by federal deputy Kim Kataguiri (Mission-SP) on Tuesday, the 18th.

item.title: Lula convoca ministros para discutir bets e taxa das blusinhas em reunião na Alvorada
item.description: President Lula convened ministers to discuss regulating bets and repealing the 'blusinhas tax,' a 20% levy on international purchases the government seeks to abolish via a provisional measure before the 2026 elections. The measure expires on September 8, and the government is pushing to establish a mixed congressional committee by September 1 to avoid opposition obstruction that could damage Lula’s electoral prospects. The issue previously split the government in 2024 and is seen as a potential liability for Lula’s re-election if unresolved.

item.title: Lula diz que petróleo brasileiro pode ser opção se Trump fechar Ormuz
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil's Margem Equatorial oil discovery could serve as a global alternative if the Strait of Hormuz is closed due to U.S.-Iran tensions. He emphasized the region's strategic importance for national and global energy security, linking exploration to Brazilian sovereignty. Petrobras has already identified hydrocarbons in the area, confirming the basin's potential for future production.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro sobe em palanque ao lado de adversário de Celina e pede votos para Flávio
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro appeared on stage alongside PSD gubernatorial candidate José Roberto Arruda, an opponent of Governor Celina Leão, and urged voters to support Flávio Bolsonaro for president, signaling a reconciliation after pre-campaign tensions. The event in Brasília launched Alberto Fraga’s (PL) re-election campaign committee, during which Michelle praised Arrudo despite not endorsing him and joked about his baldness.

item.title: Lula lamenta morte de Laura Cardoso e destaca legado da atriz: 'Sua imagem estará sempre na memória de gerações'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva mourned the death of actress Laura Cardoso, aged 98, highlighting her legacy in building Brazilian theater and television. He recalled that she received the Order of Cultural Merit in 2007 and was promoted to Grand Cross in 2025, and expressed solidarity with her family and colleagues.

item.title: Caiado promete modernizar SUS com filas por gravidade e prontuário digital
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado unveiled a health government plan to modernize the SUS by organizing patient queues by severity, implementing digital health records, using AI, creating a national efficiency dashboard, and tying federal transfers to transparency and management goals. He emphasized restoring public trust in vaccines following a measles outbreak in São Paulo and advocated for science-based health policy, refraining from naming former President Bolsonaro when criticizing vaccine denialism. Caiado also accused the Lula government of distributing funds based on political alignment and acknowledged Luiz Henrique Mandetta’s role in drafting the plan without confirming a potential Health Ministry appointment.

item.title: Renan Santos defende fim da Justiça trabalhista e diz que CLT "já era"
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential candidate from the Missão party, advocated for abolishing the Labor Justice system and declared the CLT 'obsolete', proposing a work-hour-based hiring model. He criticized the PEC ending the 6×1 work scale as 'madness' and vowed, if elected, to bury the proposal and dismantle Labor Justice, claiming left-wing lobbies and the Labor Justice system hinder economic growth and worker-employer collaboration.

item.title: Analistas veem risco de ação cibernética de EUA e bigtechs em eleições
item.description: Analysts warn of the risk of cyber operations by the U.S. and big tech firms to influence Brazil’s October 2026 general elections, citing a memorandum signed by Donald Trump that authorizes unauthorized surveillance and cyber effects. They note such actions could include infiltrating personal profiles, building dossiers to favor or harm candidates, and disrupting information systems, especially given Brazil’s reliance on U.S.-owned digital infrastructure. The recommendation is for Brazil to develop its own digital infrastructure to reduce vulnerabilities.

item.title: “EUA usam cibernética para interferir em eleições no Brasil”
item.description: Experts warn of an imminent risk of U.S. electoral interference in Brazil through cyber operations and partnerships with big tech companies, authorized by a Donald Trump memorandum enabling surveillance, unauthorized system access, and manipulation of information networks. They emphasize that Brazil’s critical state systems are controlled by U.S. corporations, threatening digital sovereignty, and urge Brazil to build its own technological infrastructure to defend against such threats.

item.title: Greenpeace: Lula afasta Brasil do pacto climático com petróleo na Amazônia
item.description: The announcement of a new oil discovery in the Amazon’s Foz region has led Greenpeace Brazil to claim the country is moving away from its climate and environmental commitments, according to Mariana Andrade, coordinator of the Oceans Front. The criticism was made during an interview on UOL News, emphasizing ecological risks associated with oil exploration in the sensitive Amazon region.

item.title: Renan Santos defende acabar com Justiça do Trabalho, diz que CLT 'já era' e critica fim da 6x1
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos from the Missão party advocated for abolishing Brazil's Labor Justice system, stating that the CLT is 'already obsolete' and that labor disputes should be handled in Civil Justice. He also criticized the end of the 6x1 workweek, arguing that labor flexibility is essential for economic competitiveness.

item.title: Lula antecipa herança aos filhos na véspera da nova tributação
item.description: Lula advanced part of his inheritance to his children between 2022 and 2023, reducing his declared assets from R$7.4 million to R$4.8 million, according to Electoral Court filings. The transfers coincided with the approval of a tax reform making ITCMD (inheritance tax) progressive, but there is no evidence the move was motivated by tax avoidance.

item.title: André e Derrite dizem que defenderão pauta "anti-STF" caso eleitos
item.description: Senate candidates Guilherme Derrite (PP) and André do Prado (PL), backed by Flávio Bolsonaro, stated they will defend an 'anti-STF' agenda if elected, including proposals to impeach justices, impose 12-year terms, and raise the minimum age for entry into higher courts from 35 to 50. Although allies have advised them to avoid immediate confrontation with the Supreme Court, both candidates said they will follow the PL's direction and support reforms proposed by the São Paulo Bar Association, though they have not emphasized the issue in recent campaign appearances, focusing instead on public security and criticism of the PT.

item.title: Mendonça manda Lula tirar do ar trecho de discurso em convenção no PT da Bahia com 'pedido direto de voto'
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to remove, within 24 hours, video excerpts from a speech at the PT’s Bahia convention where he made direct appeals for votes, which may constitute illegal early electioneering. The order also applies to Bahia Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues and the national PT directory, following a complaint by the Novo Party, which argued that statements like 'vote for me' and 'elect me for a fourth time' go beyond permissible internal party mobilization and constitute explicit voter solicitation.
